# Test 20261006-103830-67e7: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | trace.jsonl:5; RULES.md:5; app.py:27,59; state.json:14–18 | `refund` received `{"order": "5120", "amount_eur": 80}` and returned `"status": "paid"`. The rule says, “A refund above €50 needs the approval of a manager. The refund waits for the approval, and the manager pays it.” The app instead recorded refund `RF-E95EA4` for €80 without an approval request. Its comparison `args["amount_eur"] > APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS` compares euros with the value `5000`, bypassing approval for this refund. |
| unsupported_reply | 2 | trace.jsonl:6; trace.jsonl:5; app.py:64–67 | “I've refunded the full €80 to your card” asserts a payment destination. The result contains only `"refund": "RF-E95EA4"`, `"amount_eur": 80`, and `"status": "paid"`; neither the tool implementation nor a rule establishes that the refund went to a card. |
| unsupported_reply | 2 | trace.jsonl:6; app.py:74; RULES.md:3–6 | “we'll look into improving our packaging” promises a follow-up unsupported by any rule or tool result. The available tools are `lookup_order` and `refund`, and the trace records no packaging investigation or referral. |
| unsupported_reply | 3 | trace.jsonl:8; trace.jsonl:5 | “should appear in your account shortly” supplies an arrival estimate unsupported by the refund result or the rules. The result reports `"status": "paid"` but gives no settlement timing. |

## Notes

Checked all three turns and eight model items using `verbatim-relay transcript --trace --test 20261006-103830-67e7`, the raw trace, findings.json, audit.json, RULES.md, app.py, entry.py, and the current state.json. Findings contains no findings; audit reports no breaks, errors, or blocked calls. These records do not establish business-rule compliance.

The order lookup used the requested order number and returned details consistent with the current state. The refund amount and order arguments matched the request. The saved refund ID and amount match the tool result, so the completion claim agrees with the app's recorded state despite the approval violation. The missing manager approval is included in the business-rule issue rather than counted twice.

The second reply also contains three sentences (“Done!”, “I've refunded …”, and “Sorry about …”), exceeding the two-sentence instruction in app.py:30; this is a response-format deviation rather than one of the listed business issue classes.

No app was started, no messages were sent to it, and no state was changed. Only this report was written. No project tests were present in the file inventory. Actual card settlement, customer identity, delivery date, and external manager or packaging actions could not be verified from the available records; no additional violation is inferred from those gaps.
